title: Laredo College's 'Alice by Heart' brings Wonderland to the stage starting Thursday
excerpt: Laredo College theater and music students bring the musical 'Alice by Heart' to the Martinez Fine Arts Center Theatre starting Thursday, Nov. 12, with four performances through Sunday and all proceeds benefiting college scholarships.
content:
Laredo College is bringing a twist on a classic tale to the stage this week, with its theater and music students performing the musical "Alice by Heart" starting Thursday, Nov. 12, according to KGNS.

The musical adapts Lewis Carroll's "Alice's Adventures in Wonderland" and "Through the Looking-Glass," with music by Duncan Sheik, lyrics by Steven Sater and a book by Jessie Nelson. It is set in the London Blitz of 1941, where a young woman named Alice Spencer recites Carroll's story to her friend Alfred, a young man dying of tuberculosis, as they shelter in an underground tube station — and the other shelter occupants become Wonderland characters including the White Rabbit, the Mad Hatter, the Caterpillar and the Cheshire Cat.

Performances are Thursday, Nov. 12, Friday, Nov. 13 and Saturday, Nov. 14 at 7 p.m., and Sunday, Nov. 15 at 2:30 p.m., at the Guadalupe and Lilia Martinez Fine Arts Center Theatre at Laredo College, 1201 W. Washington St.

Tickets are $10 for general admission and $5 for students and seniors, with all proceeds benefiting Laredo College scholarships.

The production features original costumes, music and stage work by Laredo College students. Dr. James McGinnis, the college's Director of Fine Arts, said the show is about holding on to memory through trauma — "What Alice is doing is she is trying to get Alfred to remember something because he's trying to forget," he said — and described the music as a pop sound with a darker, jazz-influenced wartime edge.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 11, 2026; kgns.tv.
